t: You're on King William Street, in the City of London, the historic nucleus and modern financial centre of the capital. This two-way street links Lombard Street at its northern end with London Bridge, which marks the start of the A3 route to Portsmouth. It's named for William IV, who was King of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1830 until his death in 1837. The third son of George III, he succeeded his brother George IV, and was the last king of the House of Hanover to rule the United Kingdom as a king, with Victoria following him.
